author: independent web SME critic subagent (claude-opus-5-5), did not author

findings.claim: Activity 2 option D explanation says that after changing the query to max-width: 768px "the base style already gives one column on a phone, and the card would still be 396 px wide inside it". That is false: (max-width: 768px) matches a 390 px viewport, so the repeat(3, 1fr) rule applies on the phone. Executed in Chromium (Playwright, 390 px viewport, body margin 16px, the page's stylesheet): with min-width the track is 358px and each card 396px (scrollWidth 412); with max-width the tracks become 108.66px x3 and each card is 146.67px (still 38 px wider than its column, scrollWidth still 412). The verdict (D does not fix the scroll) holds, but the stated reason and predicted width are wrong, and it hides the real consequence: the change flips the layout so phones get three columns and wide screens get one.

evidence.section: Media feature expressions (range features, min-/max- prefixes)

findings.recommendation: Rewrite the D explanation, e.g.: "Not quite. max-width: 768px matches the phone, so phones would get the three-column rule and wide screens one column, the reverse of what you want. Each card would still be 38 px wider than its now narrow column, so the page still scrolls. Keep the mobile-first min-width query and fix the box size."

findings.claim: Cheat sheet line `@media (min-width: 768px) { /* wider screens only */ }` puts the closing brace inside the comment-token span, so the rule's closing } is rendered in comment colour as if it were part of the comment.
findings.recommendation: Close the span before the brace: `/* wider screens only */ }`.
